title: Remediate: unbounded recursion compiling nested choice blocks (compiler/directives.py)
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/compiler/directives.py

**Finding**:
`compile_choice` -> `_compile_directive_bodies` -> `compile_directive` -> `compile_choice` form mutual recursion with no depth limit when compiling nested `choice:` blocks in a `.ravel` story file. A story file with deeply nested choices (verified reproducible at depth ~3000 using the actual compiler functions) crashes the compiler with an unhandled `RecursionError` instead of a typed `ParseError`, and on some interpreters/thread stack sizes this class of unbounded recursion can exhaust the C stack outright. Story files are an untrusted-input surface for this engine (shared/downloaded stories, or story content an attacker can influence).

**Fix suggestion**:
Add an explicit depth counter/parameter threaded through `compile_directives`/`_compile_directive_bodies`/`compile_directive`/`compile_choice`, and raise `ravel.exceptions.ParseError` (not `RecursionError`) once a configured `MAX_CHOICE_NESTING_DEPTH` is exceeded. Add a regression test compiling a synthetically deep nested-choice story and asserting a `ParseError`, not a crash.

**Acceptance**:
- Compiling a story with nested `choice:` blocks beyond the configured limit raises `ParseError` (never `RecursionError`)
- A test exercises the limit at both the boundary and one level past it
- Normal, reasonably-nested stories (e.g. examples/cloak) still compile unchanged
close_reason: Added MAX_CHOICE_NESTING_DEPTH guard so deep choice nesting raises ParseError, not RecursionError

title: Remediate: path traversal in FileSystemLoader.get_source via untrusted include: names
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/ravel/loaders.py, src/ravel/adapters/story_source.py

**Finding**:
`FileSystemLoader.get_source` (src/ravel/loaders.py) builds `filepath = Path(self.base_path) / (name + self.extension)` where `name` comes straight from an `include:` entry in a compiled `.ravel` rulebook (src/ravel/compiler/rulebooks.py: `includes.extend(get_list_of_texts(rule[1]))`), with no sanitization. `pathlib` joins an absolute-looking segment by discarding the base entirely, and `../` segments are followed normally, so a story author can write `include: ["../../../../some/other/dir/name"]` (or an absolute path) to make the loader read a file outside `base_path`, as long as a file at that resolved path plus the `.ravel` extension exists. This is now directly reachable from the new Clean-Architecture entry point, `FileSystemStorySource.load()` -> `Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader(...))`, which is the path production code uses to compile untrusted story directories.

**Fix suggestion**:
In `FileSystemLoader.get_source`, resolve `filepath` and reject (raise `ravel.exceptions.RulebookNotFound` or a new typed error) any resolved path that is not a descendant of the resolved `base_path` (e.g. compare via `Path.resolve()` + `relative_to()`/`os.path.commonpath`, not string prefix matching). Also consider rejecting `name` values containing path separators or leading `/` at the point `include:` names are collected, since a rule name is not supposed to encode a filesystem path.

**Acceptance**:
- An `include:` value that attempts to escape `base_path` (via `../` or an absolute path) fails to load instead of reading the out-of-tree file
- A regression test constructs a story tree plus a sibling file outside it and asserts the escape attempt is refused
- Existing legitimate same-directory / subdirectory includes still resolve correctly
close_reason: Reject include names that escape base_path via ../, absolute paths, or symlinks in FileSystemLoader.get_source

title: Remediate: reconcile Constitution II strict-mypy module claim with pyproject.toml
description:
**Severity**: HIGH (sp:06-analyze finding D1)
**Artifacts**: .specify/memory/constitution.md (Principle II), pyproject.toml `[tool.mypy]`, CLAUDE.md (Environment & commands), specs/002-spec-compliance/plan.md (Constitution Check row II + Technical Context), every US1/US2/US4 Green leaf's "Strict mypy module" line
**Problem**: Constitution II says `ravel.engine.*`, `ravel.app.*`, `ravel.adapters.*`, `ravel.cli`, `ravel.types` and `ravel.queries` are strict per-module (`check_untyped_defs`, `disallow_untyped_defs`, `disallow_incomplete_defs`, `disallow_any_generics`, `warn_return_any`, `strict_equality`) and points at "the mypy override block in pyproject.toml". That block does not exist: pyproject.toml has only the `ignore_missing_imports` override, and CLAUDE.md says "no per-module override sets it". `git log -S disallow_untyped_defs -- pyproject.toml` finds nothing, so it never existed. plan.md marks Principle II PASS and the 002 Green leaves say "fully annotate" for these modules, but nothing enforces it: an unannotated function in types.py still passes `uv run mypy`.
**Probe (2026-09-28)**: adding the override block exactly as Principle II words it gives 43 errors in 3 files (`src/ravel/types.py`, `src/ravel/queries.py`, `src/ravel/cli.py:142`). `ravel.engine.*`, `ravel.app.*`, `ravel.adapters.*` are already clean under it.
**Fix (needs David's call)**:
  (A) Recommended, and the constitution-compliant option: add a `[[tool.mypy.overrides]]` block to pyproject.toml for exactly those six module patterns with exactly those six flags (not `disallow_untyped_calls`), annotate the 43 errors with no behavior change, and fix CLAUDE.md's "no per-module override sets it" sentence. Best done before US1 rewrites types.py/queries.py, or right after it, since US1 touches most of the offending lines.
  (B) Amend Constitution II (a separate, explicit constitution update, not done by sp:06) to say which modules are actually strict. This weakens a stated gate.
**Acceptance**: `uv run mypy` passes with the strict override block present (A), or the constitution and CLAUDE.md describe the real config (B); constitution II, pyproject.toml, CLAUDE.md and plan.md agree; 100% branch coverage and pre-commit still clean.
**Skills**: /pytest-unit-testing (no behavior change; run ./runtests.sh), /sp-commit
